version.changelog:
Version 1.0.2

- Updated SKILL.md with a new metadata block for better environment and dependency specification.
- Simplified and clarified the Quick Start section, using variable placeholders for reproducibility.
- Streamlined instructions to focus on single-paper reading and category specification.
- Removed the workflow and project structure details from documentation for a more concise guide.
- Added clear requirements for essential environment variables.

llm.summary: The skill's functionality (fetch arXiv papers and send them to an LLM for deep reading) is coherent, but packaging and metadata inconsistencies plus undeclared environment access and an unpinned pip install step raise caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description align with its code: it fetches arXiv papers, parses LaTeX, and uses an LLM to generate reading notes. Requested LLM-related env vars (LLM_API_KEY, LLM_BASE_URL, temperature, max tokens) are expected. However, registry metadata/README claims 'instruction-only' / 'no install spec' while the bundle contains multiple Python modules and a requirements.txt — an inconsistency in packaging/metadata (not necessarily malicious, but confusing).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and code will fetch full paper text (including LaTeX source) and transmit it to the configured LLM endpoint. That is consistent with the stated purpose, but it means potentially large amounts of paper content (and any sensitive strings present in those sources) will be sent to the remote LLM. The loader also reads local skills/ reading_prompt files and injects them as system prompts, which will affect LLM behavior (expected, but worth noting).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The registry lists no formal install spec, but SKILL.md instructs users to pip install -r requirements.txt. This will pull packages from PyPI (langchain, langchain-openai, arxiv, arxiv-to-prompt, etc.). Using pip with unpinned packages (and a package with no pinned version 'arxiv-to-prompt') is a moderate supply-chain risk: packages may execute code at install time and pull further dependencies. No arbitrary URL downloads or extracted archives are present in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The declared required env vars are LLM_API_KEY, LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_TEMPERATURE, LLM_MAX_TOKENS — these are appropriate. However, the code reads additional environment variables that are not listed in requires.env (e.g., LLM_MODEL, ARXIV_CATEGORIES, ARXIV_MAX_RESULTS, FETCH_LOOKBACK_DAYS, SKILLS_DIR from config.py). The skill therefore uses more configuration from the environment than the metadata advertises. This discrepancy can surprise users and should be documented. The primary credential is LLM_API_KEY only (proportional to purpose).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request system-wide persistence or attempt to modify other skills. It does not appear to write agent-level config or require elevated privileges. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (platform normal) but not combined with other high-risk flags here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says: download arXiv papers, parse LaTeX, and send content to an LLM to generate notes. Before installing, consider:

- Protect your LLM API key and only supply it to services/endpoints you trust; the skill will transmit entire paper text (including LaTeX) to the configured LLM_BASE_URL.
- The package includes a requirements.txt and SKILL.md tells you to pip install; pip installs execute code at install time — review requirements.txt and consider pinning versions or inspecting packages (notably 'arxiv-to-prompt') before running.
- The package reads additional env vars (LLM_MODEL, ARXIV_*, FETCH_LOOKBACK_DAYS, SKILLS_DIR) that were not listed in the skill metadata; be aware these settings can change behavior.
- The repository contains many local 'reading_prompt' files that are loaded as system prompts — if you modify or add files under skills/, they will influence the LLM prompts and outputs.

If you are comfortable trusting the LLM endpoint and the PyPI packages, proceed; otherwise, review the code (especially requirements.txt and any third-party packages) and run in an isolated environment (or with a limited API key) first.
